entries.why_wrong: Calling `f.read()` again won't pull in more data — the first call already reads the file to its end, so a second call just returns an empty string. The actual defect here isn't about how much gets read, it's that the file object itself is never closed after `read()` finishes.

Returning `f` instead of `data` would hand back the file object rather than its contents, which breaks the function's purpose of returning config text — and it still leaves the file unclosed. The bug isn't about which variable gets returned, it's that nothing ever closes the handle before (or after) the function exits.

`open(path)` already defaults to text read mode (`'r'`), so no second argument is required for this to work correctly. The real issue lives after the read succeeds: the opened file is never closed, so the descriptor leaks on every call.
